title: Anomaly Detection with Score Distribution Discrimination

problem.claim: Anomaly detection methods increasingly seek to leverage a small number of labeled anomalies together with abundant unlabeled data.

gap.claim: Existing anomaly-informed methods depend on manually predefined score targets and are vulnerable to anomaly contamination in unlabeled data while lacking adaptation to different data scenarios.

narrative_sequence.summary: Recent anomaly detection research uses a handful of labeled anomalies alongside abundant unlabeled data.
Anomaly-informed methods use manually predefined score targets to discriminate between normal and abnormal data.
These methods may be vulnerable to contaminated unlabeled data and may not adapt across data scenarios.

source_observation.claim: Manually predefined score targets can make anomaly-informed detection vulnerable to unlabeled-data contamination and different data scenarios.

interpretation.claim: Detection objectives may need to account for uncertainty in unlabeled data and variation across scenarios.

application.claim: When designing semi-supervised anomaly detection methods, evaluate sensitivity to contamination and scenario changes rather than relying only on fixed score targets.

exception.claim: The supplied source units do not establish whether this design implication holds beyond the described methods or scenarios.
